title: Vegetable Moussaka
subtitle: Layered aubergine and potato in a baked tomato and bechamel sauce
excerpt: Layers of aubergine, potato, and spiced tomato sauce topped with a thick bechamel crust. Bake until deep gold and let it rest before you cut into it.
sourceNotes: Greek moussaka tradition, adapted without meat. Layered vegetable and bechamel approach is standard across Greek home cooking.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions once fully cooled. Reheat from frozen at 180C for 30 minutes, covered with foil.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble the day before and refrigerate unbaked. Add 10 minutes to the bake time.

content.text: Vegetable moussaka keeps all the layers of the original. Aubergine and potato soak up the spiced tomato sauce as they bake. The bechamel must be thick enough to sit on top without sinking.
Heat the oven to 180C. Toss the aubergine rounds in 2 tablespoons of olive oil and season well. Spread on a baking tray and roast for 20 minutes until soft and golden. Set aside.
Parboil the potato rounds in salted water for 5 minutes. They should be barely tender, not cooked through. Drain and pat dry.

Heat the remaining 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat. Soften the onion for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, cinnamon, and oregano and cook for 1 minute. Stir in the tomato puree, then add the tinned tomatoes. Simmer for 10 minutes until thick. Season with salt and black pepper.

Make the bechamel. Melt the butter in a medium saucepan. Add the flour and stir over a medium heat for 2 minutes. Gradually whisk in the warm milk, a little at a time. Keep whisking until the sauce is smooth and thick, about 5 minutes. Remove from the heat and stir in the parmesan and nutmeg. Let it cool slightly, then beat in the eggs.
Layer the potato rounds across the base of a deep roasting tin. Spoon over half the tomato sauce. Lay all the aubergine in an even layer. Spoon over the remaining tomato sauce.
Pour the bechamel evenly over the top. Smooth with a spatula.
Bake for 40 minutes until the top is deep gold and the sides are bubbling. Rest for 15 minutes before cutting. It slices cleanly once it settles.

items.symptom: The bechamel sinks into the sauce layer.
items.cause: The tomato sauce was too loose, or the bechamel was too thin.
items.fix: Cook the tomato sauce until it holds a spoon mark. Make the bechamel thick enough to coat a spoon heavily before pouring.

items.cause: The oven runs hot or the tin is too close to the top element.
items.fix: Cover loosely with foil for the first 25 minutes, then remove to finish browning.

items.symptom: The aubergine is bitter or watery.
items.cause: The aubergine went in without roasting first, or it was not drained properly.
items.fix: Always pre-roast the aubergine before layering. It removes moisture and concentrates the flavour.
